observation: Architecture critique caught 3 CRITICALs invisible to a passing test suite: false AH3-Strategy-port precedent, unspecified session-less tool execution, and a CAS crash-orphan hole. All were contract/boundary errors a green test run would never surface. Reinforces producer/evaluator split value (CC-009). One revision round 6->8/10.

Negative/boundary ACs (AC5 User Sovereignty: no tool use / no external action) repeatedly ship 'proven by construction + code review' without an executable assertion (also AH5, AJ1). Review-fix added a tools:[] assertion this run. Candidate process rule: a negative-property AC must carry >=1 executable assertion even when the path isn't fully exercised.

Design-binding miss recurs: approved.md specified an amber alert glyph + iconBg token on the blocked EmptyState; builder shipped without it; code review (not tests) caught it. Third instance of 'plan names a primitive/token to reuse, builder misses the binding' (cf L13, U6/U7). Tests assert testids/copy but not visual-token bindings.

Low-overhead run: ~16 commits, 1 architecture revision loop, 0 blocking code-review findings, 42/42 tests green first full run, no green-phase split. Tight upstream constraints (AK1 vocab locked, AK2 port shape locked) narrowed AK3 scope and kept rework minimal. Contrast with AK2's 33% infrastructure overhead.

Orchestrator's untracked progress file (.pipeline/progress/AK3.json in shared main checkout) was removed mid-run by a concurrent git op and recreated twice. In-flight progress files aren't committed until ship, so they're vulnerable to other agents' git operations in the shared checkout. Candidate: checkpoint into worktree branch earlier or an agent-private path.
